definition: National Credit Union Administration (NCUA) is an independent federal agency that charters, regulates, and supervises federal credit unions and administers federal share insurance for federally insured credit unions. It operates under the Federal Credit Union Act. The agency is managed by the NCUA Board, which consists of three members appointed by the President with the advice and consent of the Senate. No more than two Board members may belong to the same political party. Organizers of a proposed federal credit union submit an organization certificate to the Board; when the Board approves it, the certificate becomes the credit union's federal charter. NCUA examines insured credit unions, issues regulations, and may take supervisory or enforcement actions to address unsafe or unsound practices, legal violations, or other risks. Its powers include cease-and-desist orders, removal or prohibition orders, civil money penalties, and conservatorship. State-chartered credit unions remain subject to their state chartering and supervisory authorities, while NCUA administers federal share insurance and exercises federal supervisory and enforcement authority over federally insured state-chartered credit unions. NCUA administers the National Credit Union Share Insurance Fund (NCUSIF). The fund protects eligible share accounts at federally insured credit unions up to the applicable insurance limits; coverage may also extend to non-member deposits when permitted by law. Its obligations are backed by the full faith and credit of the United States. Coverage is calculated by ownership category, and qualifying accounts in distinct categories, such as individual, joint, retirement, and certain trust accounts, may be insured separately under the share-insurance rules. When an insured credit union fails, NCUA may function as conservator or liquidating agent, pay insured account claims, arrange transfers of assets or liabilities, and manage or dispose of failed-credit-union assets. NCUA share insurance is a separate system from Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) insurance, which generally applies to insured bank deposits rather than credit-union shares.
